mainTopic: The end of שמואל's rule about which flowing river can purify (only the פרת in תשרי), his father's practice for his daughters' immersion, and the start of a new teaching from רב on the 'כלי גולה' of יחזקאל.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a rule from the previous amud about using flowing water for טבילה. Flowing river water is not good for immersion, except the פרת, and only in the days of תשרי. That is when the river clearly comes from its source and is not mixed with rain and snow. Next comes a short story: שמואל's father built מקוואות for his daughters in ניסן, and in תשרי he laid mats in the river so they could immerse there. His practice matches the rule exactly. Then a new teaching begins. רבי אמי, quoting רב, explains the 'כלי גולה' (exile equipment) that יחזקאל was told to prepare. The list starts with a lamp and a bowl and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the פרת in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ruling: the only flowing river that can be used for טבילה is the פרת, and only during תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: …except the פרת, during the days of תשרי only.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rule that began just before this point. Among flowing rivers, only the פרת works for טבילה, and only in the days of תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water that flows can purify only if it comes from a spring source. Rain and melted snow purify only when the water is standing still. In תשרי, after the dry summer, the river water clearly comes from its source. In other seasons, rain and snow mix into it, so a person cannot immerse in it while it is flowing.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of תשרי, which comes right after the dry summer

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that started before this section. The word אֶלָּא ('except') only makes sense together with the earlier part: 'flowing water does not purify, except…'

phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier sentence: flowing water does not purify, except the פרת.

phrases.english: during the days of Tishrei only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ruling that began in the text just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flowing river water can be used for טבילה only in the פרת, and only during the days of תשרי.

steps.title: שמואל's father and his daughters' immersion
steps.stepSummary: A story of practice: שמואל's father made מקוואות for his daughters in ניסן and put mats in the river for them in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father made ritual baths for his daughters in the days of ניסן, and mats in the days of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells what שמואל's father actually did. His practice matches the rule in Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ניסן the river is full of rain and snow water, so it cannot purify while it flows. That is why he built separate מקוואות of standing water. In תשרי his daughters could immerse in the river itself. He spread mats there so the mud on the riverbed would not count as a barrier (חציצה) between their bodies and the water.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of ניסן, the rainy and snow-melt season
Mats, made of reeds or woven material

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule in action. The same river is not fit for immersion in ניסן but is fit in תשרי.
steps.whatToRemember: The פרת works for טבילה in תשרי but not in ניסן. That is why שמואל's father built מקוואות in ניסן and only laid mats in the river in תשרי.

phrases.english: Shmuel's father made ritual baths for them
for his daughters in the days of Nisan,
and mats in the days of Tishrei.
phrases.notes: The word 'made' carries over here: in תשרי he set up mats in the river itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל עֲבַד לְהוֹן מִקְווֹאוֹת לִבְנָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real-life practice that fits the rule just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ניסן, build separate מקוואות. In תשרי, a person may immerse in the river, with mats laid down against the mud.

steps.title: The 'exile equipment' in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching: רבי אמי, quoting רב, explains that the 'כלי גולה' in יחזקאל's פסוק means a lamp and a bowl. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רב: What is meant by the verse, 'And you, son of man, make for yourself implements of exile'? This means a lamp and a bowl…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching. רב explains which items count as the 'exile equipment' that יחזקאל was told to prepare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say which items are meant. רב names them: the basic things a person takes along into exile, starting with a lamp and a bowl. The list is not finished here and goes on in the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written: a standard opening for explaining a פסוק
Exile equipment, the items a person takes when going into exile

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאַתָּה בֶן אָדָם עֲשֵׂה לְךָ כְּלֵי גוֹלָה״
phrases.english: "And you, son of man, make for yourself implements of exile"
— this is a lamp and a bowl

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַב מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic that does not follow from the immersion discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'כלי גולה' of יחזקאל are basic travel items, beginning with a lamp and a bowl.
